_comment: MEASUREMENT ARTEFACT, not an enrichment index. Research output only: measured hit rates for street-level and geo-image sources against a fixed-seed stratified sample of 210 arcade coordinates (30 each across Japan, United States, United Kingdom, Taiwan, Philippines, Singapore, China). Contains NO image URLs for shipping. Bottom line: no source here is worth building. Do not wire this into data/enrichment.json.

sample.note: 30 per country gives roughly plus/minus 17 points at 95 percent confidence on a mid-range rate. Differences under about 15 points between countries are not significant; the order-of-magnitude conclusions below are far outside that band.

headline.question: Can street-level imagery give each arcade a real storefront picture?
headline.answer: No. Measured usable storefront yield is 0 of 7 best-case frames inspected. The best street-level source (KartaView) reaches only 5.2 percent of arcades with a camera even pointed at the venue, and every one of those frames is a road-forward dashcam shot of asphalt. Japan and China, 58 percent of the dataset, measure 0-3 percent on every source tested.
headline.recommendation: Do not build any of these five sources.

mapillary.reason: Every endpoint is token-gated and no account is available to this agent. graph.mapillary.com/images returns HTTP 500 MLYApiException code 190 'Invalid OAuth 2.0 Access Token'. tiles.mapillary.com vector tiles return HTTP 403 both with an empty access_token param and with none.
mapillary.licence: CC BY-SA (Terms s3(b)). Some datasets are CC BY-NC-SA, whose terms take precedence where they conflict.
mapillary.attribution_required: Terms s11 does not specify a text string. It requires visibly displaying the Mapillary logo and linking back to the Mapillary homepage or the corresponding image page. Note s7 restricts trademark use, so the press-kit logo asset is needed. CC BY-SA separately requires per-image author, licence and link.
mapillary.token_note: Terms require a unique client_id per application (s2a) and forbid permitting others to access your account. Committing a token to a public MIT repo is inconsistent with both. NOT permitted, do not ship one.
mapillary.mirroring_allowed: Self-hosting individual images is contemplated by s11, but s5 prohibits automated data-gathering and bulk extraction by default, and share-alike still attaches to any mirrored image.
mapillary.china: Mainland uploads are legally precarious under Chinese surveying and mapping law and Meta services are blocked in-country, so coverage is thin. Not worth pursuing regardless of token.
mapillary.expected_if_unblocked: Mapillary is the larger of the two crowd-sourced street-level archives, so its radius hit rate would beat KartaView's. That does not change the recommendation: the binding constraint measured here is not radius coverage but that dashcam frames do not show storefronts, and Mapillary is the same windshield-mounted capture model.

kartaview.note_on_endpoints: api.kartaview.org/2.0/ returns 404; the working host is api.openstreetcam.org. An empty result is a normal HTTP 200 with apiCode 601 and result:null, not an error.
kartaview.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (imagery). Server backend is proprietary.
kartaview.attribution_required: CC BY-SA 4.0 per image: author/username, the licence name with a link to the 4.0 legalcode, and a link to the source photo. Share-alike means these images stay BY-SA; the repo's MIT licence does NOT relicense them. Any index would have to carry per-image attribution fields, not just URLs.

camera_actually_facing_venue_within_60m.definition: photo within 60 m AND camera heading within 60 degrees of the bearing from camera to venue

visual_verification.method: took every arcade meeting the best-case filter (closest photo, within 60 m, camera bearing within 60 degrees of the venue), downloaded the JPEGs and looked at them
visual_verification.verdict: All 7 are road-forward windshield dashcam frames dominated by asphalt, traffic, dashboard and sky. Two were shot at night or into the sun. None shows the arcade. This is the number that matters: radius hit rate overstates usable coverage by roughly an order of magnitude.

360_panorama_check.rationale: a 360 sphere sees sideways regardless of heading, so it is the one case where a nearby capture could still show a storefront
360_panorama_check.verdict: 360 coverage is a Singapore-only artefact (25 of 26 hits). Inspected one: it does show the containing mall facade (Bugis+), but heavily fisheye-distorted at car level, and the arcade itself is inside on an upper floor. Would need reprojection and cropping per image and still would not be a storefront shot.

kartaview.freshness: Of 252 photos within 60 m, shot years spread 2016-2025 with the mass in 2018-2019 and 2023. A material share are 6-9 years old.
kartaview.blurring: autoImgProcessingResult=BLURRED on the frames seen; faces and plates are blurred, storefront signage is not deliberately obscured. Not the limiting factor here.

wikimedia_commons.licence: per-file and mixed (CC BY, CC BY-SA, PD and others). Must be read per file via the API; there is no blanket licence.
wikimedia_commons.attribution_required: per file, per its own licence. Cannot be generated from the geosearch response alone.

name_or_address_token_match.caveat: THIS NUMBER IS AN ARTEFACT, recorded so nobody re-derives it and believes it
name_or_address_token_match.why_it_is_wrong: Inspecting which tokens matched shows they are town names pulled from the address, not venue names: 'london', 'harlow', 'southport', 'walsall', 'ormskirk'. Only 2 of the 12 UK matches inspected matched a token from the arcade NAME, and both of those were also town names (Harlow, Chatham). The high UK and Singapore figures are geography, not venue identification.

what_the_hits_actually_are: Las Vegas Amusements (UK): promenade, parish church, level crossing, seafront hotels
Tenpin Harlow (UK): Harlow Bus Station plus three photos of buses
TOCA Social (UK): O2 Arena Christmas tree, Brooklyn Bowl, a Paddington Bear statue
VIRTUALAND BUGIS+ (SG): four photos of Uniqlo clothing racks inside Bugis+
PACO FUNWORLD i12 (SG): show cars, a BYD M6 and a Maserati Ghibli
GiGO Tokyo Dome City (JP): Tokyo Dome, a baseball manager statue
GiGO Akihabara Bldg 5 (JP): a piece of public art, generic Akihabara streetscapes
China venues: metro station exits, a railway station, city skylines and night HDR panoramas
wikimedia_commons.confidence_level_of_this_finding: TITLE-LEVEL ONLY, weaker than the KartaView finding. Commons files were classified by their titles; no Commons image was downloaded and viewed. This is explicitly a lower standard of proof than the KartaView result, where 7 JPEGs were downloaded and inspected by eye. Titles like 'Bugis+ Uniqlo clothes' or 'Harlow Bus Station' are conclusive on their face, but titles like 'Miuraya.jpg' or 'Beishu.jpg' at 68 m are unclassifiable without opening them, and some of those could be the building the arcade sits in. Confirming or refuting the useful-mall-photo case would require per-image inspection, which was NOT done.
wikimedia_commons.verdict: The 59 percent raw rate is the most misleading number in this report. Commons geosearch measures 'is this a photographed place', which correlates with dense tourist and transport geography, not with arcades. Title-level classification shows the hits are dominated by transport infrastructure, vehicles and landmarks; the filtered remainder includes a clinic, a furniture store, a parked Nissan Sylvia and a municipal building. NO hit was confirmed to be the venue, though absence of confirmation here is title-level inference rather than the visual proof obtained for KartaView. This does not change the recommendation: at 50.5 percent raw-minus-noise with Japan at 37 percent and China at 7 percent, and with no per-venue certainty, Commons cannot deliver 80 percent storefront coverage, which is what the owner asked for.

osm_tags.query: nwr[leisure=amusement_arcade](around:150,lat,lng) per sampled coordinate, batched one request per country
osm_tags.licence: ODbL for the OSM data itself. An image=* URL points off-site and carries whatever licence that third-party host imposes, which is usually all-rights-reserved and NOT mirrorable.

global_ceiling.note: amenity=arcade is effectively not a real tag. 8880 worldwide objects against our 13502 arcades caps coverage below full even before asking how many carry an image.

positive_control_on_the_zero.why: a 0 of 210 is the same shape as the false zero the Switzerland extract produced, so the extraction path had to be proven capable of reporting a non-zero
positive_control_on_the_zero.conclusion: The extraction path works and DOES report image=* when present. The 0 of 210 is a real finding, not a query bug. The true global ceiling for OSM image=* is 24 objects worldwide, i.e. 0.27 percent of mapped arcades and 0.18 percent of our 13502.
positive_control_on_the_zero.and_they_are_unusable_anyway: Of the 24, the image URLs point to Google Photos share links, pagesjaunes.fr, yadi.sk, shorturl.at, private CDNs and an OVH bucket. These are third-party all-rights-reserved hosts, not mirrorable, many are shorteners or will rot. Even the 24 are not shippable under the licence position.

osm_tags.verdict: Decisive. About a third of arcades have a mapped OSM arcade object nearby, but ZERO of 210 carry image=* or wikimedia_commons=*. OSM knows where arcades are; it does not hold pictures of them. China is 0 percent even for the object itself.

what_those_P18_images_actually_are: Taito -> 'Square Enix HQ (Shinjuku Eastside Square).jpg' (a corporate office tower, not an arcade)
Taco Bell -> 'Tacobellheadquartersirvine.jpg' (a head office in Irvine; also, Taco Bell is not an arcade)
Chuck E. Cheese -> a cropped logo/sign shot
Dave & Buster's -> one specific Springfield Town Center entrance, wrong for every other branch
Tom's World -> one specific Keelung store, wrong for every other branch
chain_check.verdict: Brand P18 is actively harmful. Applying it would put a photo of Square Enix's Shinjuku head office on every Taito arcade in Japan and a Virginia storefront on every Dave & Buster's. That is worse than no image.

wikidata_p18.verdict: Hard ceiling 0.24 percent even if every one of the 74 items matched an arcade of ours. Not viable, and the chain-level fallback is wrong-building imagery.

china_datum_check.question: Are data/arcades.json China coordinates WGS-84 or GCJ-02? If GCJ-02, every China number above would be off by 500 m and meaningless.
china_datum_check.answer: WGS-84, confirmed. China numbers are trustworthy.
china_datum_check.code_evidence: scrapers/geocode_cn.py lines 647-648 run every provider result through eviltransform bd2wgs/gcj2wgs before it reaches the cache.
china_datum_check.empirical_evidence: Reverse-geocoded five random China arcade coordinates against WGS-84 Nominatim. All five returned the correct province, city and district, and one resolved to the exact named building (淄博市客运中心, matching our address). Applying gcj2wgs a second time would move them 514-626 m, confirming they are already converted.
china_datum_check.consequence: China's 0 percent street-level coverage is real, not a datum artefact.

methodology_warnings: overpass.osm.ch is a SWITZERLAND-ONLY extract. It answers HTTP 200 with zero elements for every non-Swiss coordinate. A first OSM run against it produced a plausible-looking but entirely false 0/210 across all seven countries. Control query proving this: node(around:200,35.6580,139.7016) returns 0 there and 3096 on a worldwide instance. ALWAYS run a known-good control before trusting an Overpass mirror.
The final OSM run asserts a control (Akihabara box returns 13 arcades) before measuring, and aborts otherwise.
overpass-api.de, overpass.kumi.systems and overpass.private.coffee were all returning 504 during this session. maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass worked. overpass.osm.jp fails TLS verification.
A radius hit is NOT a storefront photo. Every radius-based rate in this file overstates usable coverage; the only honest numbers are the visually verified ones.
Wikidata class Q2593535 is NOT amusement arcade (it returns 0 items). The correct class is Q260676.
